description: ZALF publishes spatial classifications of arable land in Brandenburg, Germany, for food-supply and land-use planning. The BonaRes repository map shows the named dataset and CC BY; DataCite specifies CC BY 4.0 and lists CSV and File Geodatabase formats. The describing Data article identifies three shapefile layers: climate-robust land, high-yield land from dynamic modelling, and land with high yield under both static and dynamic criteria. The classification combines soil quality and drought, water-erosion and wind-erosion risks with bio-economic crop-yield simulations under future climate conditions. Modellers can use the layers to compare agricultural land protection, renewable-energy siting or climate-adaptation scenarios across Brandenburg. These are model-derived planning classes, not observed future yields or proof that a field will stay productive. The current direct map export and the exact spatial resolution were not checked, and no geospatial file was downloaded. The catalogued German crop-type maps describe actual crop patterns in earlier years; they are related but do not duplicate this planning classification.
